title: Focusrite Control / ASIO driver missing
fullDescription: Windows needs the Focusrite USB driver from focusrite.com/downloads. Generic class-compliant mode works on macOS but Windows requires the driver for ASIO. Reinstall cleanly after uninstalling older versions.

fixSteps.title: Uninstall old version first
fixSteps.instruction: Control Panel > Uninstall Focusrite USB driver before reinstalling.

videoSearchQuery: Focusrite Scarlett driver not loaded fix

faq.a: For mixer control yes; audio itself is class-compliant.

title: 48V button unresponsive
fullDescription: Scarlett 4th Gen uses per-channel 48V via controllable buttons and the Focusrite Control 2 app. Long-press to arm; short tap selects channel. Bus-power limits can prevent 48V from activating on unpowered USB hubs.

fixSteps.title: Use direct USB port or powered hub

title: DAW reports buffer under-run
shortDescription: Audio glitches due to buffer too small.
fullDescription: Latency-focused setups run 32-64 samples. Heavy plugin chains overrun the buffer. Raise buffer size to 256-512 for mixing sessions.

causes.cause: Buffer too small for CPU load

faq.a: Typical workflow; change between tracking and mix.

title: DAW and OS sample rate disagree
shortDescription: Project opens at wrong rate or produces pitch shift.
fullDescription: If macOS Audio MIDI Setup is 48kHz but DAW opens 44.1 project, Scarlett may resample or glitch. Set OS to match project; use project-rate settings in DAW.

fixSteps.title: Match in Audio MIDI Setup
fixSteps.instruction: Set Scarlett output to project rate.

fixSteps.title: Enable 'Follow DAW'
fixSteps.instruction: Focusrite Control 2 > Follow DAW sample rate.

videoSearchQuery: Focusrite Scarlett sample rate mismatch fix

faq.a: Yes, Scarlett supports up to 192 kHz.

title: Interface not enumerating
fullDescription: USB handshake failures stem from bad cables, USB 2.0 vs 3.0 port behavior, or BIOS/firmware issues. Try the supplied cable on a direct USB-A or USB-C port.
whenToCallPro: If interface fails on multiple computers.

faq.a: 4th Gen ships USB-C; use the supplied cable.

title: Signal clipping at input
fullDescription: Scarlett's green/red Gain Halo turns red on peaks. Reduce gain, use 4th Gen's Auto Gain feature which sets level from a test take.

fixSteps.title: Run Auto Gain (4th Gen)
fixSteps.instruction: Long-press Auto; play a loud passage.

videoSearchQuery: Focusrite Scarlett Auto Gain clipping fix

faq.a: No, 4th Gen added Auto Gain and Clip Safe.

title: Direct Monitor and DAW monitor both on
shortDescription: Vocal appears twice with slight delay.
fullDescription: If Direct Monitoring is enabled on Scarlett and the DAW also routes the input back, you hear a duplicated signal. Disable one.

causes.cause: Both hardware and software monitoring enabled

fixSteps.title: Turn off software input monitor in DAW
Or disable Direct Monitor
fixSteps.instruction: Hardware button off if you want latency-compensated plugin monitoring.

videoSearchQuery: Focusrite Scarlett direct monitor echo fix

faq.a: Direct = zero latency; software = plugin effects.

title: Scarlett MIDI not listed
fullDescription: 4i4 and 8i6 include DIN MIDI. If DAW does not see them, install the Focusrite driver (Windows) and restart DAW after connection.
symptoms: No Scarlett MIDI in DAW list

fixSteps.title: Restart DAW
fixSteps.instruction: Close and reopen after plugging Scarlett in.

title: Outputs silent despite meters moving
fullDescription: Common causes: monitor knob off, headphone not selected, OS output routed elsewhere, or Focusrite Control routing matrix wrong on larger interfaces.
videoSearchQuery: Focusrite Scarlett no sound from monitors fix

faq.a: Check separate HP knob; it is independent.

title: macOS Sonoma/Sequoia USB audio quirks
shortDescription: Recent macOS updates cause intermittent crackles.
fullDescription: Certain macOS releases introduced USB audio stability regressions. Focusrite publishes firmware/driver updates; install the latest, and use a USB-C to USB-C cable directly to M-series Mac port.
